entries.sourceClaim: The slide’s augmentation blocks mix M as a landmark count with M as a state dimension; this question explicitly uses M 2D landmarks.
entries.qualification: The old state has 2M coordinates and the new landmark adds two, so every covariance dimension is 2M+2.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide prints Gx=∂g/∂x_v as an all-zero matrix in ideal localization; the derivative itself is nonzero.
entries.qualification: Knowing a variable exactly removes its uncertainty contribution, not the mathematical dependence of the inverse model on that variable.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide writes arctan(dy/dx), which needs quadrant handling; this item explicitly uses atan2.
entries.qualification: atan2(dy,dx) uses both coordinate signs and returns 135° for the second quadrant.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide prints a two-element noise Jacobian beside scalar measurement noise; this question explicitly uses the dimensionally consistent scalar noise model.
entries.qualification: The two state variances contribute 0.5+1, and measurement variance adds 0.25, giving 1.75.

entries.sourceClaim: The printed posterior off-diagonal is 0.143; direct multiplication and the Joseph covariance form both give 2/7≈0.285714.
entries.qualification: The first row of I−K H is (5/7,2/7), so multiplying by diag(0.5,1) gives the cross entry 2/7.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide’s most-recent-correlations wording can suggest that EKF forgets prior information; its current joint distribution summarizes past updates.
entries.qualification: Filtering compresses historical information into the current joint estimate; graph methods represent multiple poses and their constraints explicitly.

entries.sourceClaim: The slide prints a planar matrix with both off-diagonal sine entries positive; the question states the standard counterclockwise convention.
entries.qualification: The standard rotation sends the +x unit vector to (cos a,sin a) and preserves orthonormal axes with determinant +1.

entries.sourceClaim: The slides pass from a transform residual to fᵀΩf without defining the minimal vector representation; this question makes that required convention explicit.
entries.qualification: A planar residual can be represented by three coordinate errors; Ω must act on that vector in the same convention.

entries.sourceClaim: The introduction broadly says SLAM requires depth sensing and is unsuitable for resource-constrained robots; these are not universal requirements.
entries.qualification: The appropriate method depends on sensors, algorithms, hardware and the task; the motivation is not a universal impossibility result.

entries.sourceClaim: The same slide emphasizes texture rather than color but also lists hue, saturation and luminosity; preserve the combined-feature interpretation.
entries.qualification: The slide lists both color and texture attributes, so the distinction is from color-only matching, not a prohibition on color.

entries.sourceClaim: The figure labels v=300 as the horizon although its own level-camera equation and principal point imply v=200.
entries.qualification: The fraction tends to zero, so the horizon for this level-camera equation is v0=200.

entries.sourceClaim: The slides describe reliable safe regions and ensuring collision-free motion; those phrases do not prove safety under all real sensing and motion conditions.
entries.qualification: An appearance classification is only one input to a physical safety decision and depends on several assumptions.

additionalScope: Source code examples were reconstructed and executed with official PyPI RTB 1.4.4; the original Lecture45 notebook was not found in the checked course directory.
Map colors without legends are not assigned invented occupancy meanings.
Static landmark corrections change estimates, not physical objects.
Topological maps can be augmented with metric attributes; the bare graph distinction is explicit.
A generalized pose-landmark graph differs from a pure pose graph.
Floor-finding perspective calculations assume calibrated level camera, flat floor and floor-contact points.
Pixel erosion is not a substitute for physical robot-clearance validation.
